provenance.title: NeRF: Representing Scenes as Neural Radiance Fields for View Synthesis
provenance.abstract: We present a method that achieves state-of-the-art results for synthesizing novel views of complex scenes by optimizing an underlying continuous volumetric scene function using a sparse set of input views. Our algorithm represents a scene using a fully-connected deep network, whose input is a single continuous 5D coordinate (x,y,z,theta,phi) and whose output is the volume density and view-dependent emitted radiance at that location.
key_claims: Represents continuous scenes as 5D neural radiance fields parameterized by a single MLP, mapping (x,y,z,theta,phi) to (RGB, sigma)
Introduces a differentiable classical-volume-rendering procedure to optimize the MLP directly from posed RGB images without 3D supervision
Introduces a high-frequency positional (Fourier feature) encoding that lets the MLP represent high-frequency geometry/appearance, overcoming networks' spectral bias toward low frequencies
Proposes a two-stage (coarse+fine) hierarchical sampling strategy that concentrates ray samples on visible scene content for sampling efficiency
Outperforms prior neural/volumetric view-synthesis baselines (SRN, Neural Volumes, LLFF) on synthetic and real forward-facing benchmarks while requiring only ~5MB of network weights per scene

architecture.primary_variant: Full NeRF (positional encoding + view-dependence + hierarchical coarse/fine sampling)

modules.name: PositionalEncoding_x

parameters.function: gamma(p) = (sin(2^0 pi p), cos(2^0 pi p), ..., sin(2^(L-1) pi p), cos(2^(L-1) pi p))

modules.notes: Applied independently to each of the 3 coordinate components of x.

modules.name: MLP_Trunk (F'_Theta, spatial branch)

parameters.skip_connection: gamma(x) input is concatenated into the activation of layer 5 (DeepSDF-style skip)

modules.notes: Density sigma is predicted as a function of position x only, enforcing multiview consistency.

modules.name: DensityHead
modules.notes: Emitted together with an un-activated 256-d feature vector that feeds the color branch.

modules.name: ColorHead (view-dependent branch)
modules.notes: Concatenates the trunk's 256-d feature vector with the encoded viewing direction before one ReLU layer and a final sigmoid layer producing RGB.

modules.name: CoarseNetwork (F_theta_coarse)
modules.input_shape: 5D coordinate (x, d) sampled via stratified sampling
modules.notes: Structurally identical to the shared MLP_Trunk/DensityHead/ColorHead architecture; a separate weight instance is optimized for the coarse pass.

modules.name: FineNetwork (F_theta_fine)
modules.input_shape: 5D coordinate (x, d) sampled via coarse-weighted importance sampling, union of Nc+Nf points
modules.notes: Second, separately-weighted instance of the same MLP architecture; evaluated at the union of coarse stratified samples and new importance samples.

modules.name: HierarchicalSampler
modules.input_shape: coarse weights w_i (from Eq. 5), Nc samples along ray
modules.output_shape: Nf additional sample locations along ray, biased toward high-weight regions
modules.notes: Weights w_i are normalized into a piecewise-constant PDF; Nf new samples are drawn via inverse-CDF sampling.

modules.name: VolumeRenderer
modules.input_shape: sequence of (c_i, sigma_i, delta_i) along a ray
modules.notes: Reduces to classical alpha compositing with alpha_i = 1 - exp(-sigma_i * delta_i).

variants.name: Full model (No PE/VD/H ablation baseline excluded)

mathematical_spec.name: Stratified sampling of ray parameter t
Coarse-network ray-color weights / hierarchical sampling PDF
Normalized Device Coordinate (NDC) ray reparameterization for forward-facing real scenes

datasets.name: Real Forward-Facing (LLFF + authors' captures)
datasets.split: 20-62 images per scene, 1/8 held out for test, 8 scenes, 1008x756px

evaluation_protocol.compute: Single NVIDIA V100 GPU per scene; 100k-300k iterations, ~1-2 days training per scene; ~30 sec/frame render at test time (150-200 million network queries per rendered image)
special_conditions: A separate network is trained per individual scene (not a generalizable/amortized model)
SRN baseline evaluated at lower resolution (512x512 or 504x376) due to GPU memory limits, vs 800x800/1008x752 for other methods

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Reference framework is TensorFlow 1.x (as used by the original authors)
implementation_assumptions.basis: Explicitly stated in paper Appendix A: 'We implement our model in Tensorflow'
alternatives: PyTorch reimplementation (common in later community ports, including TinyNeRF)

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Weight initialization is standard framework default (e.g. Glorot/Xavier for FC layers) since the paper does not specify an initialization scheme
implementation_assumptions.basis: common practice for MLPs of this era

implementation_assumptions.assumption: No explicit data augmentation is used beyond the natural stochasticity of random ray/pixel sampling and stratified sampling along rays
implementation_assumptions.basis: Paper describes only random ray-batch sampling; no image-space augmentation (crop/flip/color jitter) is mentioned
alternatives: none plausible given the requirement for exact posed-image photometric supervision

implementation_assumptions.assumption: For a consumer-hardware-friendly reproduction (per user request, e.g. 4GB VRAM), adopt principles from the official community 'TinyNeRF' notebook (bmild/nerf tiny_nerf.ipynb): single MLP (no separate coarse/fine networks), fewer/smaller layers, downsampled images (e.g. 100x100), a single stratified-sampling pass with no hierarchical importance sampling, and a much smaller iteration count for fast demonstration.
implementation_assumptions.basis: External community reference implementation, not part of the original paper's methodology -- included because the user explicitly requested consumer-hardware optimization inspired by TinyNeRF
alternatives: Keep the full coarse+fine two-network paper-faithful architecture but reduce batch size / image resolution / iteration count to fit VRAM
Use gradient checkpointing or mixed precision (not in the original paper) to fit the full model on 4GB VRAM

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Scene bounding volume / near-far planes (t_n, t_f) must be supplied per-dataset; assumed to be the synthetic-scene bounding cube [-1,1]^3 for synthetic data and NDC-mapped [0,1] disparity range for real forward-facing data, matching Appendix B/C
implementation_assumptions.basis: Explicitly described in Appendix B ('Volume Bounds') and Appendix C (NDC derivation)
alternatives: manually tuned per-scene near/far planes from COLMAP depth estimates

implementation_assumptions.assumption: Random Gaussian noise (zero mean, unit variance) is added to raw sigma outputs before the ReLU only when training on real scene data, as a regularizer
implementation_assumptions.basis: Explicitly stated in Appendix A ('Training Details') as specific to real scene data
alternatives: applying the same noise regularization to synthetic data as well

ambiguities.description: The paper states iterations 'typically take around 100k-300k' to converge but does not give one fixed number of training steps used for the headline results.
Learning-rate decay is described as 'begins at 5e-4 and decays exponentially to 5e-5 over the course of optimization' without stating the exact decay rate/step schedule.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: exponential decay with decay computed so that lr reaches 5e-5 at the final training step (standard exponential schedule: lr = lr0 * (lr_end/lr0)^(step/total_steps))
alternatives: cosine decay to the same end value

ambiguities.description: It is not fully explicit whether the coarse and fine networks are two entirely independently-initialized/parameterized MLPs of identical architecture, or whether any parameters are shared between them.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Two fully independent MLP instances of identical architecture, both optimized jointly (no weight sharing)
alternatives: partial weight sharing (e.g. shared early layers)

ambiguities.description: TinyNeRF (bmild/nerf tiny_nerf.ipynb) is an external, non-peer-reviewed community/author demo notebook, not part of the NeRF paper itself. Its exact hyperparameters (image size ~100x100, single MLP depth, iteration count ~1000-5000) are not verifiable from the paper text and must be sourced separately if faithfully reproduced downstream.
ambiguities.primary_assumption: Treat TinyNeRF-inspired settings purely as an optional 'consumer-hardware' architecture variant layered on top of the paper-faithful SIR, not as a modification of the paper's own reported methodology or results
alternatives: Fetch and parse the actual tiny_nerf.ipynb notebook content in a later stage to pin down exact hyperparameters
